A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CBS scaling study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original C4 language-model training experiments, fitted CBS scaling laws, scheduler comparisons, and optimization ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports additional weight-decay and CBS-threshold sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The architectures, Adam-based training, constant-learning-rate plus EWA procedure, and principal CBS estimation approach remain unchanged. Weight decay remains disabled for the principal experiments; its new evaluation is an ablation.

E1.justification: Both versions study autoregressive language-model pre-training on C4, retaining the context-length and under-/over-training investigations. The added weight-decay and threshold checks introduce no new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Cosine, WSD, and schedule-free optimization remain the evaluated scheduler comparators against Constant+EWA, including in the corresponding appendix panels. Newly cited works are not added empirical baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds weight-decay sweeps at learning rates 0.01 and 0.00316 and evaluates CBS using 10% and 50% overhead thresholds alongside 20%. Its scheduler comparison ends at batch size 4096 rather than 8192. Principal model settings, target-loss selection, and validation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds an ablation testing whether disabling weight decay affects CBS, and Appendix E adds sensitivity to the overhead threshold. Scheduler analyses are revised, while the existing context-length, width/depth, momentum, warmup, and EWA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D retains the same evaluation-set variance measurements and sample counts. Neither version adds training-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing.

E6.justification: v3 reports overhead-sensitivity exponents of 0.48 and 0.44 for 10% and 50% thresholds, and little CBS effect from weight decay. Scheduler curves are replaced, and the batch-8192 comparison is removed. The principal CBS fits and Tables 6–7 remain unchanged; the revised curves do not establish a controlled performance gain.

T1.justification: The formal results and Appendix G proofs are retained, with theorem and corollary statements moved into Section 4.2. However, new informal Corollary 1 asserts 0 < c < 1/2 in the variance-dominated regime. This is not generally implied by the retained exponent 1-a/min{b,2a+1}, which can exceed 1/2.

C1.justification: The central claim that CBS scales primarily with data size remains. The introduction narrows the claimed literature gap from lacking a formal CBS definition to lacking a formalism relating model and data sizes. It also replaces the compute-for-speed trade-off wording with an assertion of greater parallelism without FLOPs-efficiency loss.

C2.justification: The scheduling takeaway changes from outperforming cosine at large batches to competitive performance. v3 explains disabling weight decay through its limited CBS effect and explicitly attributes width/depth-associated CBS growth to increased data. The conclusion removes the earlier future-work qualifications concerning heterogeneous data and extreme model/data ratios.

D1.justification: v3 discloses cosine duration multipliers, schedule-free beta1 choices, the PyTorch weight-decay implementation, and scipy.optimize.fsolve usage. Table 3 better explains defaults and selective sweeps. These disclosures do not by themselves establish changes to existing experiments; hardware and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds a substantive comparison with concurrent Filatov et al. (2024), distinguishing model-scale coverage and theoretical support. It also adds references concerning EWA optimization, scheduler connections, weight decay, and parallelism, while retaining the overall research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially reorganized into empirical takeaways and theoretical implications. Section 4.2 now presents the detailed risk theorem and corollary previously in Appendix G. Experimental-design explanations, scheduling discussion, the conclusion, and several appendix passages are also rewritten.

P2.justification: Former Figures 1 and 6 become a six-panel Figure 1 with reordered control panels. Figure 2 is redrawn as one panel, appendix scheduler plots are redrawn, context/width figures are reordered, and a weight-decay figure is added. Several Figure 1 references retain the old middle/right ordering.

improvement.justification: The added weight-decay and threshold-sensitivity checks modestly strengthen empirical support, while clearer tuning and fitting details improve reproducibility. These gains are limited by incorrect Figure 1 panel references, the new inconsistent informal exponent bound, and removed scope qualifications. The principal findings and formal proofs remain stable, supporting a limited overall improvement.
